learn.title: Smart Grids and Advanced Metering
learn.intro: Smart grids use digital technology to monitor and manage electricity flow in real time, enabling two-way communication between utilities and consumers. This modernization supports renewable integration, reduces outages, and empowers users to make informed energy choices.
learn.c1_text: Smart grids digitize the power system using sensors, meters, and software. Think of them like a highway traffic control system—adjusting flow based on demand. In Italy, smart meter adoption helped reduce peak demand by 5%, showing how real-time data improves efficiency.
learn.c2_text: Advanced meters record usage every 15 minutes, sending data wirelessly to utilities. Unlike traditional meters read monthly, these provide granular insights. In the U.S., over 90% of households now have smart meters, enabling dynamic pricing and faster outage detection.
learn.c3_text: India launched its National Smart Grid Mission in 2013 to modernize its grid. Over 250 million smart meters are planned under the Smart Meter National Infrastructure Company (SMNIC). This supports renewable integration and reduces commercial losses, which currently exceed 20% in some states.
learn.stat1: Over 1.7 billion smart meters installed globally (IEA, 2023)
learn.stat2: Smart grids can reduce outage duration by up to 30%
learn.stat3: India aims to install 250 million smart meters by 2025
learn.stat4: Digital grid investments reached $500 billion globally in 2022

learn.title: Floating Solar Farms on Water
learn.intro: Floating solar farms generate clean energy while conserving water by reducing evaporation. Installed on reservoirs and lakes, they avoid land competition and benefit from cooler temperatures, boosting efficiency. This innovation is especially valuable in water-scarce regions.
learn.c1_text: Floating solar panels sit on water bodies, saving land and reducing water evaporation by up to 70%. They also run cooler, increasing output by 5–10% compared to ground-mounted systems. China's 320 MW Dezhou Dingzhuang project is among the world's largest.
learn.c2_text: In arid regions, floating solar helps preserve freshwater. A 1 MW floating array can save around 2.5 million liters of water annually. In drought-prone areas like California, this dual benefit makes floating PV a climate-resilient solution for energy and water security.
learn.c3_text: India plans 40 GW of floating solar capacity by 2030. The 600 MW Ramagundam project in Telangana is among the largest under development. With over 90 potential sites identified, India leverages its vast water bodies to scale solar without using farmland or forests.
learn.stat1: Global floating solar capacity reached 1.2 GW in 2021 (IRENA)
learn.stat2: Floating PV systems show 5–10% higher efficiency than land-based ones
learn.stat3: India targets 40 GW of floating solar by 2030
learn.stat4: A 1 MW floating array can save 2.5 million liters of water per year

learn.title: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Technology
learn.intro: Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) allows electric vehicles to feed electricity back into the grid during peak demand. With millions of EVs expected on roads, V2G turns parked cars into mobile energy storage units, enhancing grid stability and creating new revenue streams for drivers.
learn.c1_text: V2G enables bidirectional charging—EVs both draw power from and supply power to the grid. A Nissan Leaf with a 30 kWh battery can power an average home for a day. When aggregated, fleets of EVs act as virtual power plants, balancing supply and demand in real time.
learn.c2_text: V2G supports frequency regulation and peak shaving. During high demand, EVs discharge stored energy, reducing strain on power plants. In South Korea, a V2G pilot with 600 Kia Ray vans provided 3.2 MW of flexible capacity, proving the concept at scale.
learn.c3_text: India plans to electrify 30% of private vehicles by 2030. If 10% of EVs support V2G, they could offer 20 GW of flexible capacity. Pilot projects by Tata Motors and IIT Bombay are testing feasibility. Policy frameworks are needed to unlock V2G's full potential in India.
learn.stat1: Over 1 million EVs globally support bidirectional charging (IRENA, 2022)
learn.stat2: A Nissan Leaf can supply up to 6 kW of power via V2G
learn.stat4: V2G could provide 20 GW of flexible capacity in India by 2030

learn.title: Hydrogen Fuel Cells in Vehicles
learn.intro: Hydrogen fuel cells generate electricity through a chemical reaction between hydrogen and oxygen, emitting only water. Ideal for long-haul transport and heavy industry, they complement batteries in sectors where weight and refueling speed matter most.
learn.c1_text: In a fuel cell, hydrogen passes over a catalyst, splitting into protons and electrons. Electrons flow through a circuit, creating electricity. Unlike combustion, this process is silent and produces no CO₂—just water vapor. Toyota Mirai and Hyundai Nexo are commercial examples.
learn.c2_text: Fuel cell vehicles refuel in under five minutes and travel over 500 km per tank. They’re ideal for trucks, buses, and trains. In California, over 40 hydrogen stations serve 18,000+ fuel cell vehicles. Heavy-duty transport accounts for 20% of transport emissions.
learn.c3_text: Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, India plans to introduce hydrogen buses and trucks. Indian Oil is developing hydrogen refueling infrastructure. Tata Motors and Mahindra are testing fuel cell trucks. Green hydrogen production will scale with solar and wind capacity.
learn.stat1: Over 18,000 fuel cell vehicles on roads globally (US DOE, 2023)
learn.stat2: Hydrogen refuels in under 5 minutes vs. 30+ minutes for fast-charging batteries
learn.stat3: Heavy-duty transport contributes 20% of global transport emissions

learn.title: India's National Green Hydrogen Mission
learn.intro: Launched in 2023, India's National Green Hydrogen Mission aims to make the country a global leader in clean hydrogen production. With $2.3 billion in funding, it targets 5 MMT of annual green hydrogen production by 2030, transforming energy, industry, and exports.
learn.c1_text: The mission targets 5 million metric tons (MMT) of green hydrogen annually by 2030. It plans to attract $3 billion in investment and create 330,000 jobs. Green hydrogen will decarbonize steel, chemicals, and transport sectors while positioning India as an export hub to Europe and Asia.
learn.c2_text: India offers production-linked incentives (PLI) up to ₹300 crore per project. The government allocates ₹19,700 crore ($2.3 billion) over five years. Additionally, tax breaks on electrolyzer imports and duty exemptions on capital goods support domestic manufacturing and cost reduction.
learn.c3_text: The mission promotes domestic electrolyzer manufacturing. Reliance and Adani are investing heavily in green hydrogen parks. India plans 10 large-scale projects with total capacity of 2.5 GW by 2026. This aligns with its 500 GW renewable target by 2030.
learn.stat1: India targets 5 MMT green hydrogen production by 2030
learn.stat2: Mission allocates ₹19,700 crore ($2.3 billion) in funding
learn.stat3: 330,000 jobs expected to be created by 2030
learn.stat4: 10 large-scale projects planned with 2.5 GW capacity by 2026

learn.title: Green Ammonia as Clean Fuel
learn.intro: Green ammonia is produced using renewable-powered electrolysis to split water into hydrogen and oxygen, then combining hydrogen with nitrogen. It serves as a zero-carbon fuel for shipping and a clean alternative for fertilizers, addressing hard-to-abate sectors.
learn.c1_text: Green ammonia starts with renewable electricity splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen via electrolysis. Hydrogen then reacts with nitrogen from air under high pressure. Unlike grey ammonia made from fossil fuels, green ammonia emits no CO₂ when produced or used.
learn.c2_text: Ammonia contains 17.6% hydrogen by mass, making it an efficient energy carrier. In shipping, it can replace heavy fuel oil. Yara and MAN Energy are developing ammonia-powered engines. By 2050, ammonia could meet 15% of global shipping fuel demand, per IEA estimates.
learn.c3_text: India plans to become a top green ammonia exporter. Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, 10 mega projects are proposed. Companies like Reliance and IOCL are investing in production hubs. Target: 5 MMT annual capacity by 2030 for domestic use and exports.
learn.stat1: Green ammonia can store 17.6% hydrogen by mass
learn.stat2: Global ammonia demand expected to reach 230 million tons by 2050
learn.stat3: India plans 5 MMT annual green ammonia capacity by 2030
